# DocStash MCP — tools

The tools the DocStash MCP server advertises to a connected agent, with the
exact descriptions and input schemas the agent receives. Reads and mutations
first, then the authoring tools.

---

## `list_documents`

List the user's documents. By default returns ACTIVE docs in their default organization (team org if they have one, personal otherwise). Use `which` to switch lens:
  • 'active'         — default. Docs the user owns or is an org member on. Has the user's own work.
  • 'trash'          — recently-trashed docs. Use when the user says "what did I delete" / "restore X" / "undelete".
  • 'shared-with-me' — docs OTHER people shared with this user (cross-org grants).

Returns slug, name, url, type, language, owner attribution, and latest-version summary for each. Use this to find an existing doc's `slug` before calling `read_document`, `manage_document`, `manage_sharing`, or an authoring tool.

**Hints:** `{"title":"List documents","readOnlyHint":true,"destructiveHint":false,"openWorldHint":false}`

### Input schema

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "which": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "active",
        "trash",
        "shared-with-me"
      ],
      "description": "Which list to return. Default: 'active'."
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": true
}
```

## `get_pdf`

DISPLAY a PDF to the user inline by slug — renders OFF your context (bytes go to the widget, nothing enters the conversation; returns metadata + an artifact reference, never the text). Use when the user asks to SEE a doc ("show / open / pull up X"). To load the TEXT into your context to summarize or revise, use `read_document` instead. `get_pdf` shows only a PDF; a wrong-type call names the right tool.

**Hints:** `{"title":"Show PDF","readOnlyHint":true,"destructiveHint":false,"openWorldHint":false}`

### Input schema

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "slug": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The doc's 6-char slug (from `stash` / `list_documents` / URLs)."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "slug"
  ],
  "additionalProperties": true
}
```

## `read_document`

Read a document's CONTENT into your context by slug — a SILENT read: NOTHING is rendered or shown to the user (no widget, no preview, no link card). This is the right FIRST call whenever you need the text to reason over — to summarize it, answer questions about it, or edit it into a new version (edit → then call the matching create_* tool with this SAME slug).

Returns the doc's metadata, a reference to its latest artifact (id, signed fileUrl, metadata), `content` — the full body text — for text-like kinds (html/md/text + agent-authored pdf print-HTML + the xlsx/docx specs; binary uploads aren't text-extractable), and any unresolved lint `errors` on the latest version (this is ALSO the way to re-check errors mid-fix-loop — no separate errors tool).

Pass `withHistory: true` to also include the activity feed — every event newest-first (type, timestamp, author, and for content_pushed events the `artifactId` used by manage_document action='revert'). To DISPLAY the doc to the user instead, call the matching `get_*` show tool (get_pdf / get_page / get_sheet / …) — it renders inline entirely off your context.

**Hints:** `{"title":"Read document","readOnlyHint":true,"destructiveHint":false,"openWorldHint":false}`

### Input schema

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "slug": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The doc's 6-char slug (from `stash` / `list_documents` / URLs)."
    },
    "withHistory": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "If true, also include the activity history (event feed with artifact ids) in the response."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "slug"
  ],
  "additionalProperties": true
}
```

## `screenshot_document`

SCREENSHOT a staged document by slug — the rendered result comes back AS IMAGES for your own review, plus the deterministic `errors`. Renders the latest pushed version and returns:
  • `errors` — problems detected at render time. PDF: fixed-page geometry (text past the page edge, content wider than its own box or table cell, text-on-text overlap, content overprinting a bottom-pinned footer, broken images, off-page/clipped elements, blank pages, an underfilled page with a big blank band, sub-legible text, a page scaled down to fit). HTML/APP: viewport + runtime checks (horizontal blowout on desktop or mobile, missing viewport meta, broken images, a blank render, uncaught boot exceptions, missing bundle files, console errors). ALL advisory — nothing blocks a stash; fix them when iterating, never by stripping design.
  • screenshots delivered to YOU as image content — PDF: one per page, up to 8 pages per call. A bare call serves pages 1-8; pass `firstPage`/`lastPage` to pick pages yourself (the user says "pages 5-8 are broken", or you want the next window of a longer doc). When the doc has more pages than one call ships, the result names the range sent (`pageRange`) — keep calling with new ranges until you have seen every page you need. Everything else: a bounded full-height shot at DESKTOP and at MOBILE (390px) — so you can SEE the result and catch what the checks cannot: hidden text, wrong colours, a broken visual layout.

Call it after authoring or iterating a PDF, page, or app to check your work BEFORE telling the user it is ready — especially when a create tool reported errors. The images return to YOU (the model); they are NOT the user-facing inline widget.

**Hints:** `{"title":"Screenshot document","readOnlyHint":true,"destructiveHint":false,"openWorldHint":false}`

### Input schema

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "slug": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The doc's 6-char slug (from a create_* result / list_documents / a docstash URL)."
    },
    "firstPage": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 1,
      "description": "PDF only, optional: 1-based first page of the range to screenshot — use when specific pages need review (the user says \"pages 5-8 are broken\") or to fetch the next window of a longer doc. Omit for the first 8 pages."
    },
    "lastPage": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 1,
      "description": "PDF only, optional: 1-based last page of the explicit range (defaults to firstPage — a single page). At most 8 pages ship per call."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "slug"
  ],
  "additionalProperties": true
}
```

List members of the user's default organization — their names AND emails. Use this to figure out WHO TO SHARE WITH when the user says "share with the team" / "who's on this organization?" / "share with Alice" (and you need to resolve Alice → email).

## `manage_document`

Doc-level actions other than upload. Pass the `slug` plus an `action`:

  • 'rename'  — change the doc's name. Requires `name`. No new version minted (metadata only). Use when the user says "rename X to Y".
  • 'trash'   — soft-delete. Doc disappears from active list, shows up in `list_documents` with which='trash'. RECOVERABLE — don't tell the user it's permanently gone.
  • 'restore' — un-trash. Mirror of 'trash'. Find the slug via `list_documents` with which='trash'.
  • 'revert'  — repoint the doc at an EARLIER artifact. Requires `artifactId` (get it from `read_document` with withHistory:true — each content_pushed event carries `payload.artifactId`). No bytes move; the server bumps that artifact's refCount and logs a content_pushed event. History stays intact.

For UPLOADING content (create a new doc, push a new version), use the separate `stash` tool — NOT this one.

**Hints:** `{"title":"Manage document","readOnlyHint":false,"destructiveHint":true,"idempotentHint":false,"openWorldHint":false}`

### Input schema

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "slug": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The doc's 6-char slug."
    },
    "action": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "rename",
        "trash",
        "restore",
        "revert"
      ],
      "description": "Which action to perform on the doc."
    },
    "name": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Required when action='rename'. The new name (up to 200 chars)."
    },
    "artifactId": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Required when action='revert'. The full id of the artifact to revert to (from `read_document` with withHistory:true)."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "slug",
    "action"
  ],
  "additionalProperties": true
}
```

## `manage_sharing`

Share AND PUBLISH a doc — this is the ONLY tool that makes a doc public. Use it to PUBLISH / make public / get a public shareable link (action='set-public', isPublic=true), and to grant/revoke per-user access. Pass `slug` + `action`:

  • 'list'        — list all per-user grants (Viewers + Editors). Does NOT include public-link state (use `read_document` for that — it's on `document.isPublic`).
  • 'add'         — grant a specific person access. Requires `email`. Optional `level: 'read' | 'write'` (default 'read'). The recipient must be a DocStash user (sign in once at app.docstash.ai). NOT a public link.
  • 'revoke'      — revoke a per-user grant by `email`. Mirror of 'add'.
  • 'set-public'  — PUBLISH / unpublish the doc: toggle its PUBLIC LINK. Requires `isPublic: boolean`. true = PUBLISH — anyone with the URL sees the latest version (anonymous, no sign-in); false = revoke the public link. This is the ONLY way to make a doc publicly viewable — a bare stashed url stays private. The doc must be saved (stashed) first; you can't publish an unsaved version. Per-doc only — no version-pinned public links.

Call this when the user explicitly asks to PUBLISH, make public, get a public/shareable link, or share/revoke per-user access. Don't infer sharing from vague phrasing like "can you give Alice access" without checking what level they want.

**Hints:** `{"title":"Manage sharing","readOnlyHint":false,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":false,"openWorldHint":true}`

### Input schema

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "slug": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The doc's 6-char slug."
    },
    "action": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "list",
        "add",
        "revoke",
        "set-public"
      ],
      "description": "Which share operation."
    },
    "email": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Required when action='add' or 'revoke'. The grantee's email."
    },
    "level": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "read",
        "write"
      ],
      "description": "Optional, only meaningful when action='add'. 'read' (Viewer) or 'write' (Editor). Default 'read'."
    },
    "isPublic": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "Required when action='set-public'. true = enable public link; false = revoke."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "slug",
    "action"
  ],
  "additionalProperties": true
}
```

## `create_pdf`

Generate a beautiful, print-ready PDF document for DocStash and show the user an INLINE PREVIEW: reports, memos, proposals, letters, résumés, whitepapers, contracts, essays, one-pagers. THIS IS THE DEFAULT for a generic 'make me a document' / 'make me a PDF' request (use `create_docx` only when the user specifically wants an editable WORD doc, `create_text` for markdown/code source, `create_page` for a web page). `content` = a complete self-contained `<!doctype html>` document — you author it in HTML/CSS and DocStash renders + presents it AS A PDF (paginated paper, page nav, zoom, one-click PDF download). Do NOT generate a binary .pdf; the user drag-and-drops pre-existing .pdf files on the dashboard.

This is a REAL HTML/CSS/JS document rendered by a full Chromium engine and baked to PDF — you have the SAME toolkit a web page has (any CSS layout, SVG, gradients, filters, web fonts, images, JS), NOT a limited document format. The ONLY difference from a live web page is GEOMETRY: it is a fixed A4 sheet that never scrolls or reflows. The structural rules below cover that fixed page.

PAGE CONTRACT — a PDF is a stack of FIXED A4 sheets (794×1123px @96dpi), not a reflowing web page. Emit one `<div class="ds-page">…</div>` (or `<section class="ds-page">`) per page — N pages, N blocks. YOU own pagination: nothing reflows across pages, so author each page to the ~1123px sheet and, when content runs long, SPLIT it into more `.ds-page` blocks yourself and decide where the breaks fall.

STRUCTURE EACH PAGE WITH REGIONS (recommended) — mark semantic bands and DocStash lays them out for you:
  • `.ds-content` — the body. Wrap each page's content in it. It fills the region BETWEEN the header/footer bands; if it overruns that region, DocStash shrinks THE CONTENT (only) to fit — a `squeezed` WARNING, not an error, so pace your pages so you rarely hit it and never rely on it. Content is bounded to its region, so it can't collide with the bands.
  • `.ds-header` / `.ds-footer` — pinned top/bottom bands (optional, recommended for multi-page docs). Declare them ONCE at the TOP LEVEL (a `.ds-header` / `.ds-footer` OUTSIDE any `.ds-page`) and DocStash repeats them on every page EXCEPT the cover (page 1); a page's own band overrides, and `class="ds-page ds-no-header"` (or `ds-no-footer`) suppresses. Put `<span class="ds-pageno"></span>` / `<span class="ds-pagetotal"></span>` in a footer — DocStash fills the number / total; never hand-number pages.
  • `.ds-bg` — an optional decorative full-bleed background (image / gradient / tint) that always COVERS the sheet and never shrinks with the content; keep positional / anchored elements in `.ds-content`, not here.
  • Make page 1 an attractive COVER. A bare `.ds-page` with content directly inside (no region classes) still works — it is treated as one block that shrinks as a WHOLE if it overruns the sheet — but regions give you pinned chrome, auto page numbers, a full-bleed background, and content that can't collide, so prefer them.

DESIGN FOR THE FIXED PAGE:
  • TYPE SCALE — 794px wide = A4 210mm, so **1 CSS px = 0.75pt**: `11px` body copy PRINTS AT 8.25pt. Size in px but think in pt — body copy ≈13–15px (≈10–11pt), never below 11px for anything a reader must read; 9px (≈7pt) is the floor for incidental labels / footers.
  • FILL each page — a sheet is a WHOLE A4 page whether or not its content fills it, so a half-empty interior page reads as a mistake, not restraint. Pace and size content (type scale, spacing, columns, where you break) so every page is ROUGHLY FULL; only the FINAL page should run partial, and never orphan a lone heading or a few trailing lines. Balanced, full pages are what separate a designed document from an exported one.
  • Do NOT hard-pin `.ds-page` to `height:1123px` — let DocStash supply the A4 size (via `min-height`) so a slightly-too-tall page can breathe. Footers / page numbers ride the page bottom via the flow (or a `.ds-footer` band), not a fixed `height`.
  • Do NOT style the `<body>` background, the margins AROUND the paper, or scrolling — DocStash owns the canvas + chrome. Style only the INTERIOR of each `.ds-page`.
  • MARGINS — give body pages a comfortable margin so text never runs to the paper edge; `padding:48px` (≈13mm) on `.ds-page` is a good default, more for formal reports. As a safety net DocStash auto-applies a default margin to any page whose body content would otherwise touch BOTH side edges, so a page never prints flush by accident — but design your own margins rather than leaning on it. To bleed a page to the edge on purpose (a full-bleed cover, a background, an edge-to-edge image) set your own padding or add `class="ds-page ds-bleed"`; a full-bleed background layer (`.ds-bg`, or one element covering the whole sheet) is detected and left alone.
  • Self-contained: inline all `<style>`; load fonts / images / libraries from absolute https/CDN URLs. IMAGES & FONTS — image/font URLs MUST be DIRECT files (a gallery/viewer page renders BROKEN); the direct-URL recipes, sizing, and custom-font rules are in the server instructions (VISUAL DOCUMENTS & MEDIA). REPEATING gradient patterns (`repeating-linear-gradient`, tightly-tiled backgrounds) rasterize unreliably in print — build stripes / hatching from REAL repeated elements (divs / spans) instead.

Nothing is stashed yet — then STOP: do NOT call `stash` yourself; the user reviews the preview and saves it. Full lifecycle, slug/versioning, attribution + publish rules: DocStash server instructions.

**Hints:** `{"title":"Create PDF","readOnlyHint":false,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":false,"openWorldHint":false}`

### Input schema

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "name": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Required when creating a new doc; omit when pushing a new version (use `slug` instead)."
    },
    "slug": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Slug of an existing doc to iterate (from a create_* result, `list_documents`, or a docstash URL — a full URL is accepted). OMIT for a NEW doc; a stale slug OVERWRITES that doc. Iterate-vs-new rules: server instructions."
    },
    "description": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "One-line commit-style changelog for THIS version (≤~8 words — the CHANGE, not the whole doc), e.g. \"Add Q3 revenue table\". Set it on every call; it becomes the version-history entry."
    },
    "content": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "A complete `<!doctype html>` document, everything inline, with each page wrapped in `<div class=\"ds-page\">…</div>`. DocStash renders + presents it as a real paginated PDF — do NOT pass a binary."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "content"
  ],
  "additionalProperties": true
}
```

## `create_docx`

Generate an EDITABLE Word document (.docx) for DocStash and show the user an INLINE PREVIEW — a reflowable Word doc on a US-Letter page (1" margins). Use this when the user specifically wants a WORD doc / editable .docx; for a DESIGNED, print-perfect document use `create_pdf` instead. `content` = MARKDOWN — the renderer walks it straight to a real .docx. The browser renders it at view time — do NOT generate a binary.
  Author rich markdown (don't flatten to plain text). Mapped to native Word: headings (#..###### → real Heading styles a TOC can use), **bold**/*italic*/~~strike~~, `inline code` + ```fenced blocks```, ordered/unordered (nested) lists, tables, blockquotes, links, images (![alt](https-url), embedded at view time), ==highlight==, <u>underline</u>, footnotes (text[^1] + [^1]: note), and a page break via a lone ---pagebreak--- (or \f, or <!-- pagebreak -->). IMAGES & FONTS — image/font URLs MUST be DIRECT files (a gallery/viewer page renders BROKEN); the direct-URL recipes, sizing, and custom-font rules are in the server instructions (VISUAL DOCUMENTS & MEDIA).

Nothing is stashed yet — then STOP: do NOT call `stash` yourself; the user reviews the preview and saves it. Full lifecycle, slug/versioning, attribution + publish rules: DocStash server instructions.

**Hints:** `{"title":"Create Word doc","readOnlyHint":false,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":false,"openWorldHint":false}`

## `create_sheet`

Generate a SPREADSHEET / WORKBOOK (Excel) for DocStash and show the user an INLINE PREVIEW. `content` = JSON.stringify(SheetSpec) — do NOT generate an .xlsx binary; the browser renders real Excel at view time. Spec schema below.

Nothing is stashed yet — then STOP: do NOT call `stash` yourself; the user reviews the preview and saves it. Full lifecycle, slug/versioning, attribution + publish rules: DocStash server instructions.

XLSX SPEC SHAPE (when kind='xlsx'):
  { theme?: '<preset>' | { custom theme }, sheets: [ Sheet, ... ] }   — 1-20 sheets per workbook. A custom theme is a FLAT object (fields at top level, NOT nested under `custom`): { headerBackground, headerText, text, stripe, border, accent, font? }.
  Sheet: { name, rows: Row[], columnWidths?: number[], rowHeights?: number[], frozenRows?: number, frozenCols?: number, merges?: string[], autoFilter?: string, conditionalFormats?: CF[], charts?: Chart[] }
    • name         — tab label, ≤31 chars; avoid [ ] : * ? / and \
    • rows         — top-to-bottom; each row is an array of cells (rows may be ragged — short rows pad empty on the right)
    • columnWidths — left→right, Excel char-width units; omit to auto-fit
    • rowHeights   — top→bottom, in points; omit/null an entry to keep default height
    • frozenRows / frozenCols — sticky header rows / label columns that stay visible while scrolling
    • merges       — A1 ranges to merge, e.g. ['A1:D1','A2:A5']; top-left cell's value/format wins (great for spanning titles)
    • autoFilter   — A1 range to attach Excel filter dropdowns, e.g. 'A1:F1' (header) or 'A1:F100' (whole block)
    • conditionalFormats — declarative rules (heatmaps, bars, icons, threshold highlights); see CF below
  Cell — a BARE value for the common case, or an OBJECT when you need a formula / formatting / comment:
    bare:   string | number | boolean | null
    object: { value?, formula?, result?, format?, comment?, hyperlink?, validation? }
      • formula   — Excel formula starting '=', e.g. '=SUM(B2:B10)', '=IF(A1>0,"yes","no")', cross-sheet '=Sheet2!B5*1.1' (overrides value)
      • result    — IMPORTANT cached formula value: ALWAYS supply the computed result alongside `formula`, else many viewers show the cell BLANK until they recalc. (You may instead pass `value` next to `formula` as the cache.)
      • hyperlink — makes the cell a clickable link; its `value` is the display text
      • validation — { type:'list'|'decimal'|'whole'|'date', values?, min?, max?, allowBlank?, prompt?, error? }; 'list'+values gives a dropdown
  format (CellFormat): { bold?, italic?, underline?, strikethrough?, color?, background?, fontFamily?, align?: 'left'|'center'|'right', valign?: 'top'|'middle'|'bottom', numberFormat?, fontSize?, wrapText?, border? }
    • color / background — hex '#RRGGBB' OR a theme token (color: 'text'|'accent';  background: 'headerBackground'|'stripe'|'accent')
    • fontFamily   — per-cell font override (e.g. 'Arial','Courier New'); defaults to the theme font
    • numberFormat — Excel format string: '#,##0' int · '#,##0.00' 2dp · '$#,##0' currency · '0.00%' percent · 'yyyy-mm-dd' date · '@' force-text
    • border — per side { top?, right?, bottom?, left? }; each side is `true` (thin, theme color) OR { style?:'thin'|'medium'|'thick'|'double'|'dashed', color? }
  CF (Sheet.conditionalFormats[]): { range:'B2:B100', type:'colorScale'|'dataBar'|'iconSet'|'cellIs'|'expression', ...rule }
    • colorScale — colors?: 2-3 hex low→high (default red→yellow→green heatmap)
    • dataBar    — color?: hex bar color (default theme accent)
    • iconSet    — iconSet?: '3TrafficLights1'|'3Arrows'|'5Rating'|... (default '3TrafficLights1')
    • cellIs     — operator:'greaterThan'|'lessThan'|'greaterThanOrEqual'|'lessThanOrEqual'|'equal'|'notEqual'|'between', value, value2?(for between), background?/fontColor?
    • expression — formula:'$B2>$C2' (no leading '='), background?/fontColor? applied where TRUE
  Chart (Sheet.charts[]): { type: 'bar'|'line'|'pie'|'area'|'scatter', title?, dataRange: 'A1:B10', categoriesRange?, position: { fromRow, fromCol, cols, rows } }  — rendered as a native Excel chart in the download.
  CONVENTION — the FIRST row of each sheet is treated as the themed header. Put values/formulas as raw numbers (not pre-formatted strings) and let `numberFormat` style them, so totals/charts compute. For any `formula`, also pass its computed `result` so the workbook isn't blank on first open.
  Theme presets:
    • 'minimal' — Clean header bar (navy blue + white text), light gray stripes, sans-serif. Safe default for most data.
    • 'corporate' — Deep blue header, white text, subtle stripes, Calibri. Standard business workbook look.
    • 'finance' — Dark green header (currency-feel), white text, no stripes, Calibri. Financial models / accounting.
    • 'research' — Charcoal header, off-white text, off-white stripes, Helvetica narrow. Academic / data-research vibe.
    • 'minimal_dark' — Dark slate background throughout, light text, subtle border. Dark-mode tables.
  Minimal example (JSON.stringify this): {"theme":"finance","sheets":[{"name":"Q3","frozenRows":1,"rows":[["Item","Revenue"],["Subscriptions",{"value":42000,"format":{"numberFormat":"$#,##0"}}],["Total",{"formula":"=SUM(B2:B2)","format":{"bold":true,"numberFormat":"$#,##0"}}]]}]}

**Hints:** `{"title":"Create spreadsheet","readOnlyHint":false,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":false,"openWorldHint":false}`

### Input schema

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "name": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Required when creating a new doc; omit when pushing a new version (use `slug` instead)."
    },
    "slug": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Slug of an existing doc to iterate (from a create_* result, `list_documents`, or a docstash URL — a full URL is accepted). OMIT for a NEW doc; a stale slug OVERWRITES that doc. Iterate-vs-new rules: server instructions."
    },

      "description": "One-line commit-style changelog for THIS version (≤~8 words — the CHANGE, not the whole doc), e.g. \"Add Q3 revenue table\". Set it on every call; it becomes the version-history entry."
    },
    "content": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "JSON.stringify(SheetSpec). See the SHEET SPEC SHAPE in this tool description. Do NOT pass an .xlsx binary."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "content"
  ],
  "additionalProperties": true
}
```

## `create_app`

Generate a LIVE WEB APP (a multi-file bundle) for DocStash and show the user an INLINE PREVIEW. Use this ONLY when you're genuinely shipping MULTIPLE files (e.g. index.html + a separate app.js + styles.css + local assets). For a single self-contained page, use `create_page` instead — it has no bundle, so it can't fail on a missing local file.
Deliver the finished app THROUGH this tool — DocStash hosts the bundle live at a shareable URL. Do NOT leave it as a local file/artifact or paste the files into the chat.

Pass `files: { "path/to/file": "<contents>", ... }`; the MCP server zips in-memory and uploads as a bundle. YOU MUST declare:
  - `entry`    — the file the runtime mounts (e.g. 'index.html' for a static site, 'app.py' for a python script).
  - `language` — the RUNTIME token: 'static' (HTML+CSS+JS), 'python', 'ruby', 'php', 'lua', 'go', 'rust', 'cpp', 'java', etc.
  - `framework` — declare this WHENEVER the bundle uses any of these (lower-case, exact token): 'react' / 'vue' / 'svelte' / 'solid' / 'preact' / 'angular' / 'lit' / 'htmx' / 'alpine' / 'qwik' / 'astro' / 'three' (THREE.js / 3D animations / WebGL scenes) / 'p5' (p5.js / generative art / creative-coding) / 'd3' (D3.js / data viz / charts) / 'jquery'. Pick ONE — the primary library the app is built around. Drives the dashboard card chip.
    Examples:
      - HTML page imports Three.js to render a rotating cube → framework: 'three'
      - React app with a useState counter                   → framework: 'react'
      - p5.js sketch of bouncing particles                  → framework: 'p5'
      - Plain HTML + CSS + a tiny <script> tag, no library  → omit `framework` entirely
    Omit ONLY when the bundle uses NO known framework. Don't guess — you just generated the files, you know which library is in there. Realistic for agent-generated apps: typically 10-50 KB of text, fits in one tool call.
BUILD-FREE RULE (language='static') — the bundle is served to the browser EXACTLY as uploaded; there is NO build step. Do NOT ship a framework SOURCE project: no `.svelte` / `.vue` / `.ts` / `.tsx` files, no Vite/webpack config expecting compilation (the browser can't load those as `<script type="module">`, and DocStash won't compile them — the app fails with a 'module script … MIME text/html' error). For Svelte / React / Vue / Solid, either (a) inline a PREBUILT single bundle of plain .js/.css into `index.html`, or (b) import the framework from a CDN as ESM, e.g. `import { mount } from 'https://esm.sh/svelte'`. STRONGLY PREFER esm.sh — it serves correct, CORS-safe, versioned ESM, React included: `import React from 'https://esm.sh/react@18'` + `import { createRoot } from 'https://esm.sh/react-dom@18/client'`, mounted from a `<script type=module>`. AVOID the in-browser Babel transformer (@babel/standalone + a `text/babel` script): it's slow and the #1 runtime failure. And DON'T load React/ReactDOM from cdnjs UMD unless the path includes `/umd/` (…/react/18.2.0/umd/react.production.min.js) — omitting `umd/` 404s, the 404 HTML comes back as a non-executable script, and the app dies with 'React is not defined'.
MODULE-FORMAT CHECKLIST (these three console errors mean you authored a BUILD-STEP/bundler app the runtime can't run) — (1) `Unexpected token 'export'` / (2) `Cannot use import statement outside a module`: a file using `import`/`export` (e.g. an esm.sh module or your own code) was loaded as a CLASSIC script. EVERY file that uses `import`/`export` MUST be loaded via `<script type="module">`; a bare `<script src=…>` at an ESM module throws these. (3) `Unexpected token '<'`: a referenced local JS path (a build output like `/src/main.jsx`, `/assets/index-*.js`, or an extensionless `/client` entry) isn't in the bundle, so the static runtime SPA-falls-back and serves your index.html for that request — the browser then parses HTML as JS. NEVER reference build-output paths; only reference files you actually put in `files`, or absolute CDN URLs. If you'd hit any of these, re-author as EITHER a single self-contained page (prefer `create_page`) OR a bundle whose every script is inline or a `type=module` CDN-ESM import.
SELF-CONTAINED BUNDLE RULE — the bundle must stand alone. Every LOCAL URL your entry references (scripts, styles, images, fonts) MUST be a key in `files`. For every asset you have exactly three valid choices: (a) inline it, (b) include it in `files`, or (c) load it from an absolute CDN URL (https://…). NEVER reference a local path you didn't write. In particular, do NOT add `<link rel="icon" href="/favicon.ico">` (or any icon/manifest link) unless you actually include that file — a stray local ref is the #1 cause of broken bundles. IMAGES & FONTS — image/font URLs MUST be DIRECT files (a gallery/viewer page renders BROKEN); the direct-URL recipes, sizing, and custom-font rules are in the server instructions (VISUAL DOCUMENTS & MEDIA).

RESPONSIVE — the page MUST reflow + scroll on mobile: include the `<meta name="viewport">` tag and DON'T lock it to `height:100vh` + `overflow:hidden` (that traps phone scrolling). The viewer renders full-width, no extra scroll container.

Nothing is stashed yet — then STOP: do NOT call `stash` yourself; the user reviews the preview and saves it. Full lifecycle, slug/versioning, attribution + publish rules: DocStash server instructions.

**Hints:** `{"title":"Create web app","readOnlyHint":false,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":false,"openWorldHint":false}`

### Input schema

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "name": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Required when creating a new doc; omit when pushing a new version (use `slug` instead)."
    },
    "slug": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Slug of an existing doc to iterate (from a create_* result, `list_documents`, or a docstash URL — a full URL is accepted). OMIT for a NEW doc; a stale slug OVERWRITES that doc. Iterate-vs-new rules: server instructions."
    },
    "description": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "One-line commit-style changelog for THIS version (≤~8 words — the CHANGE, not the whole doc), e.g. \"Add Q3 revenue table\". Set it on every call; it becomes the version-history entry."
    },
    "files": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "description": "Map of relative paths → UTF-8 file contents (e.g. `{ \"index.html\": \"<!doctype html>...\", \"styles.css\": \"body { ... }\" }`). The MCP server zips everything in memory and uploads as a bundle. Paths can't start with '/' or contain '..'. SELF-CONTAINED: every local URL your entry references — scripts, styles, images, fonts, favicon — MUST be a key here; for anything you don't bundle, use an absolute CDN URL (https://…). Never reference a local path you didn't include."
    },
    "entry": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The entry file inside the bundle the runtime mounts (e.g. 'index.html', 'app.py'). Must be a path that exists in `files`."
    },
    "language": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The RUNTIME token: 'static' (HTML+CSS+JS), 'python', 'ruby', 'php', 'lua', 'go', 'rust', 'cpp', 'java', etc."
    },
    "framework": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Optional. Declare a known framework when the bundle uses one: react / vue / svelte / solid / preact / angular / lit / htmx / alpine / qwik / astro / three / p5 / d3 / jquery. Lower-case. Drives the dashboard card chip. Omit for vanilla bundles."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "files",
    "entry",
    "language"
  ],
  "additionalProperties": true
}
```

## `create_page`

Generate a WEB PAGE (a single self-contained HTML file, rendered live) for DocStash and show the user an INLINE PREVIEW: landing pages, visual/interactive dashboards, infographics, demos — anything the user should SEE RENDERED rather than read as source. Content = a complete `<!doctype html>` document with everything inline (`<style>`, `<script>`) and any images/libraries referenced by absolute URL or CDN. IMAGES & FONTS — image/font URLs MUST be DIRECT files (a gallery/viewer page renders BROKEN); the direct-URL recipes, sizing, and custom-font rules are in the server instructions (VISUAL DOCUMENTS & MEDIA). Viewer provides chrome — don't wrap.
Deliver the finished page THROUGH this tool — DocStash hosts it live at a shareable URL. Do NOT leave it as a local file/artifact or hand back raw HTML in the chat. Load any JS deps as `<script type="module">` ESM (esm.sh) or inline them — never reference a local build-output path (the file won't exist).
ROUTING: ONE self-contained page → this tool, NOT `create_app` (a single file structurally can't have broken local references; use create_app only for genuinely MULTI-FILE bundles). Markdown / source code / raw data → `create_text` (inert source, not a rendered page). A designed PDF document → `create_pdf`; an editable Word doc → `create_docx`.

RESPONSIVE — the page MUST reflow + scroll on mobile: include the `<meta name="viewport">` tag and DON'T lock it to `height:100vh` + `overflow:hidden` (that traps phone scrolling). The viewer renders full-width, no extra scroll container.

Nothing is stashed yet — then STOP: do NOT call `stash` yourself; the user reviews the preview and saves it. Full lifecycle, slug/versioning, attribution + publish rules: DocStash server instructions.

**Hints:** `{"title":"Create web page","readOnlyHint":false,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":false,"openWorldHint":false}`

### Input schema

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "name": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Required when creating a new doc; omit when pushing a new version (use `slug` instead)."
    },
    "slug": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Slug of an existing doc to iterate (from a create_* result, `list_documents`, or a docstash URL — a full URL is accepted). OMIT for a NEW doc; a stale slug OVERWRITES that doc. Iterate-vs-new rules: server instructions."
    },
    "description": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "One-line commit-style changelog for THIS version (≤~8 words — the CHANGE, not the whole doc), e.g. \"Add Q3 revenue table\". Set it on every call; it becomes the version-history entry."
    },
    "content": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "A complete `<!doctype html>` document as a UTF-8 string, everything inline."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "content"
  ],
  "additionalProperties": true
}
```

## `create_text`

Generate an INERT text artifact — markdown, source code, or raw data — for DocStash and show the user an INLINE PREVIEW. This is for content the user READS AS SOURCE (typography for markdown, syntax highlighting for code), never executed or rendered as a page. Pick `type`:
  • 'md'   — markdown. Content = the markdown source. For prose, notes, READMEs, technical docs, documentation of any kind.
  • 'text' — source code / data in ~30 formats. Content = the raw source string. Set `language` to the canonical token (python / typescript / go / rust / json / yaml / csv / sql / etc.).
ROUTING: scripts, code files, READMEs, configs, raw CSV/JSON → here. A LIVE rendered page → `create_page`. A designed PDF (and any generic 'make me a document/PDF' ask) → `create_pdf`; an editable Word doc → `create_docx`. A spreadsheet with real cells/formulas → `create_sheet` (raw CSV data stays here).

Nothing is stashed yet — then STOP: do NOT call `stash` yourself; the user reviews the preview and saves it. Full lifecycle, slug/versioning, attribution + publish rules: DocStash server instructions.

**Hints:** `{"title":"Create text or code","readOnlyHint":false,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":false,"openWorldHint":false}`

### Input schema

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "name": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Required when creating a new doc; omit when pushing a new version (use `slug` instead)."
    },
    "slug": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Slug of an existing doc to iterate (from a create_* result, `list_documents`, or a docstash URL — a full URL is accepted). OMIT for a NEW doc; a stale slug OVERWRITES that doc. Iterate-vs-new rules: server instructions."
    },
    "description": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "One-line commit-style changelog for THIS version (≤~8 words — the CHANGE, not the whole doc), e.g. \"Add Q3 revenue table\". Set it on every call; it becomes the version-history entry."
    },
    "type": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "md",
        "text"
      ],
      "description": "'md' (markdown) or 'text' (source code / data)."
    },
    "content": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The content as a UTF-8 string: markdown source for 'md'; the raw source for 'text'."
    },
    "language": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "For type='text', the canonical language token (python / json / csv / yaml / typescript / rust / etc.)."
    },
    "filename": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Optional hint for type='text' when `language` is omitted — server infers from the extension."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "type",
    "content"
  ],
  "additionalProperties": true
}
```

## `stash`

STASH a preview (from a create_* tool) — the actual SAVE; the doc stays PRIVATE. The `slug` IS the doc's slug (creates it, or pushes a new version if the preview targeted an existing doc). ‼️ Do NOT call this automatically after a create_* call — a plain 'create X' request is satisfied by the preview alone. Call it ONLY when the user signals saving (save / stash / ship it / looks good) or clicks Stash in the inline preview; when in doubt, ask first. Returns the `url`. Stashing does NOT publish — to make it public, then call `manage_sharing` action='set-public'.

**Hints:** `{"title":"Stash","readOnlyHint":false,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}`

### Input schema

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "slug": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The slug returned by a create_* tool."
    },
    "name": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Optional override for the doc name at save time (new docs only)."
    },
    "description": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Optional one-line changelog OVERRIDE. Prefer setting this on the create_* tool instead — a changelog set here is lost if the user stashes the preview manually. Only use this to override the preview's stored changelog at save time."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "slug"
  ],
  "additionalProperties": true
}
```

## `discard`

Discard a preview (from a create_* tool) without stashing it. Call this when the user rejects it (e.g. 'discard', 'never mind', 'don't save it'). Nothing was persisted; this invalidates the preview so it can no longer be stashed.

}
```

## `set_organization`

Switch the active organization that NEW documents are created in, by organizationId (from get_organizations). Persists for this connection until changed. Existing documents remain reachable by slug regardless of the active organization.

**Hints:** `{"title":"Set organization","readOnlyHint":false,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}`

      "description": "The organization id from get_organizations."
    }

  "required": [

  ],
  "additionalProperties": true
}
```
